title: Choose what to teach by its leverage
statement: Choose what knowledge to teach by its leverage (how often later texts and tests draw on it, what builds on it and how widely it transfers).
example: Frequency kept a 25% weight, only as a sanity check that makes every high-leverage outlier be defended.
detail: The reading project's topic selection for a Grade 3 course weights a reasoned leverage score at 0.75 and keeps frequency, how many of 7 expert programs teach the topic, at 25% as an external sanity check, because what the field commonly teaches is other people's design choices, not a discovered structure (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-2/approval-package-v2/sources/TOPIC-SELECTION.md`). In its worked examples the most frequently taught candidate had the lowest leverage and was rejected, and student interest was struck as a ground for keeping a topic because it tested flat as a learning driver (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-2/approval-package-v2/sources/LOAD-BEARING-METRIC.md`). Use how commonly others teach a topic only as a minor check, and don't count how interesting it seems.
against: The 0.75/0.25 weighting and the per-factor split are declared dials, not claimed as measured (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-2/approval-package-v2/sources/LOAD-BEARING-METRIC.md`, line 146), and the file does not say how interest was tested.

evidence.quote: interest tested flat as a learning driver, so it was struck from the record (Honesty log).
"what the field commonly teaches" is a set of other people's design choices, not a discovered structure, so it carries *less* authority than powerful/portable knowledge.
Frequency stays at 25% as an external sanity check that forces every high-leverage outlier to be defended.
The mirror image of Greek myth: *most* frequently taught, *lowest* leverage.
(Its earlier "cheap to generate" justification was explicitly *rejected* as non-evidence.)
Its earlier "student interest" justification was explicitly *rejected* (interest was found flat as a learning driver)
Load-bearing measures how much **other reading the knowledge unlocks**
**Load-bearing scores how much reading power a topic deposits — measured as a property of the knowledge the texts actually carry, not an abstract rating of the topic.**
